lines.en: Graffiti and street art are forms of art created on walls or public surfaces. This art is often considered illegal because it is done without the permission of the building owners.
lines.zh: 涂鸦和街头艺术是在墙壁或公共表面上创作的艺术形式。这种艺术往往被认为是违法的，因为它没有得到楼主的许可。

lines.en: These art forms have existed since the times of ancient Greece. But the more modern style began forming in the 1960s in the cities of New York and Philadelphia.
lines.zh: 这些艺术形式从古希腊时代就有了，但更现代的风格是 20 世纪 60 年代在纽约和费城开始形成的。

lines.en: "Graffiti" often appears as words -- usually the names of the artist or their art crew. Graffiti artists write the words in creative ways and with colorful spray-paint.
lines.zh: “涂鸦”通常以文字的形式出现——一般是艺术家或他们艺术团体的名字。涂鸦艺术家用彩色喷漆以富有创意的方式书写这些字。

lines.en: "Street art" is more based on images. Artists try to communicate a message through these images. Large pieces of street art are also called murals.
lines.zh: “街头艺术”更多基于图像，艺术家试图通过图像传达信息。大型的街头艺术作品也叫壁画。

lines.en: Graffiti and street art can be controversial. They are sometimes used to mark gang territory or damage someone's property.
lines.zh: 涂鸦和街头艺术可能有争议。它们有时被用来标记帮派地盘或损坏他人财产。

lines.en: Washington has tried to increase its fines for illegal graffiti. Yet it is also encouraging the creation of public art and murals.
lines.zh: 华盛顿一直在设法提高对非法涂鸦的罚款，但同时也在鼓励创作公共艺术和壁画。

lines.en: Cory Stowers is a D.C.-based graffiti and street artist. He is president of the D.C. graffiti crew Double Down Kings, or 2DK. He is also the art director for Art Bloc D.C., a local street art organization.
lines.zh: 科里·斯托尔斯是华盛顿的涂鸦和街头艺术家，也是华盛顿涂鸦团体“双倍下注之王”（2DK）的负责人，还是本地街头艺术组织 Art Bloc D.C. 的艺术总监。

lines.en: With Art Bloc D.C., Stowers is trying to create a bridge between the street art community and the D.C. public. He helps get permission from building owners to organize large mural projects around the city.
lines.zh: 斯托尔斯通过 Art Bloc D.C. 努力在街头艺术圈和华盛顿公众之间架起桥梁。他帮助从楼主那里获得许可，在全市组织大型壁画项目。

lines.en: The projects give local street artists the chance to create their art in public, without fear of breaking the law. They also give younger artists a chance to develop their skills.
lines.zh: 这些项目让本地街头艺术家有机会在公共场所创作，不必害怕违法，也让年轻艺术家有机会提升技能。

lines.en: These projects are important, Stowers says. D.C. is making it more and more difficult for graffiti street artists to get practice. Construction projects and increased security have taken away important practice spaces throughout the city.
lines.zh: 斯托尔斯说，这些项目很重要。华盛顿让涂鸦街头艺术家越来越难找到地方练习。建筑工程和加强的安保占去了城市各处重要的练习场地。

lines.en: Practice is extremely important, Stower explains. Many artists who paint popular murals in communities today got their start by painting graffiti.
lines.zh: 斯托尔斯解释说，练习极其重要。如今许多在社区里画受欢迎壁画的艺术家，都是从画涂鸦起步的。

lines.en: "There's always this conversation that you have to have with folks and explaining to them that that young person that wrote a signature on their wall 10 years ago may be the same person that they're asking to come paint a mural… Without one you don't get the other."
lines.zh: “你总得跟人们进行这样一番对话，向他们解释：十年前在他们墙上签名的那个年轻人，可能就是他们现在请来画壁画的同一个人……没有前者，就没有后者。”

lines.en: Street artists with Art Bloc D.C. ask community members for their opinions on the murals. They want to create pieces that are meaningful for local residents. Stowers says interacting with the local community helps to "humanize" graffiti and street artists.
lines.zh: Art Bloc D.C. 的街头艺术家会征求社区居民对壁画的意见。他们想创作对本地居民有意义的作品。斯托尔斯说，与本地社区互动有助于让涂鸦和街头艺术家显得更“有人情味”。

lines.en: "I think as communities start to recognize the value of public murals and they start to understand who actually can paint them, the idea of cultivating graffiti artists will become a little bit more popular."
lines.zh: “我想，随着社区开始认识到公共壁画的价值，开始了解究竟谁能画这些壁画，培养涂鸦艺术家的想法会更受欢迎一些。”

lines.en: In 2007, the city government created the program MuralsDC. The program hires artists to paint legal murals around the city.
lines.zh: 2007 年，市政府创立了 MuralsDC 项目，雇用艺术家在全市合法地画壁画。

lines.en: Nancee Lyons is MuralsDC's art director. She says the program has two goals. One is to try to prevent illegal graffiti. The other is to "beautify" the city. Program officials believe that, if murals already cover city walls, graffiti artists will not paint over them illegally.
lines.zh: 南希·莱昂斯是 MuralsDC 的艺术总监。她说这个项目有两个目标：一是防止非法涂鸦，二是“美化”城市。项目官员认为，如果城市的墙上已经有了壁画，涂鸦艺术家就不会非法在上面乱画。

lines.en: Aniekan Udofia is a D.C.-based artist. He often paints for MuralsDC, and is known for his large works of art around the city.
lines.zh: 阿尼坎·乌多菲亚是华盛顿的艺术家，经常为 MuralsDC 作画，以他在全市的大型作品出名。

lines.en: He says the logic of the program is correct. Unofficial rules in the street artist and graffiti community say that the more complex the work of art, the more priority it has on a wall. Large murals, then, often take priority over simpler graffiti art. They are usually not vandalized or damaged.
lines.zh: 他说，这个项目的逻辑是对的。街头艺术和涂鸦圈的非正式规矩是：作品越复杂，在墙上就越有优先权。所以大型壁画往往比简单的涂鸦享有优先权，通常不会被涂改或破坏。

lines.en: "... Going over a well-done beautiful mural -- it goes outside of graffiti and at that point it's just that you hate either the artist or you hate the work that has been created."
lines.zh: “……在一幅精心创作的美丽壁画上乱涂——那已经超出了涂鸦的范围，那时你要么就是讨厌那个艺术家，要么就是讨厌那件作品。”

lines.en: Udofia and his art director, Mia Duvall, agree that communicating with the local residents is very important.
lines.zh: 乌多菲亚和他的艺术总监米娅·杜瓦尔都认为，与本地居民沟通非常重要。

lines.en: "I think anything you do in a public space you have to consider the community. We have to consider who is seeing this, how it's going to affect them and what's important to them… So every piece we do, we really do our best to make sure that we are being sensitive and thoughtful about who has to see this every day and how they are going to embrace this"
lines.zh: “我认为在公共空间做任何事，都必须考虑社区。我们得考虑谁会看到它，它会怎样影响他们，什么对他们重要……所以我们做的每一件作品，都尽最大努力确保自己体贴周到，想着每天必须看到它的人以及他们会怎样接受它。”

lines.en: Udofia recently finished a major MuralsDC project. It covers one of the walls of Ben's Chili Bowl, a historic D.C. restaurant. The bright and colorful mural features 16 well-known African Americans, including Barack and Michelle Obama, Harriet Tubman, Muhammed Ali, and Dave Chappelle.
lines.zh: 乌多菲亚最近完成了一个重要的 MuralsDC 项目。它覆盖了华盛顿历史悠久的餐馆“本的辣椒碗”的一面墙。这幅色彩鲜艳的壁画画了 16 位著名的非裔美国人，包括巴拉克和米歇尔·奥巴马、哈丽特·塔布曼、穆罕默德·阿里和戴夫·查佩尔。

lines.en: The work was introduced to the public in a ceremony on June 21.
lines.zh: 这件作品在 6 月 21 日的一个仪式上向公众揭幕。

lines.en: Actor and comedian Dave Chappelle attended the ceremony. He told VOA that public art is an important part of a city's culture.
lines.zh: 演员兼喜剧演员戴夫·查佩尔出席了仪式。他告诉 VOA，公共艺术是一座城市文化的重要组成部分。

lines.en: "Public art gets right to the heart of a culture of a city… who they love, who they represent, what's the neighborhood about..."
lines.zh: “公共艺术直击一座城市文化的核心……他们爱谁，他们代表谁，这个街区是什么样的……”

lines.en: I'm Phil Dierking
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。

qs.q: What happened after the police officer arrested Gobi?
opts: He asked for Gobi's business card.
qs.a: He asked for Gobi's business card.
qs.why: "he asked Gobi for his business card."

qs.q: What are two goals of MuralsDC?
opts: prevent illegal graffiti and beautify the city
qs.a: prevent illegal graffiti and beautify the city
qs.why: "One is to try to prevent illegal graffiti. The other is to 'beautify' the city."

qs.q: What is the difference between graffiti and street art?
opts: Graffiti is often words; street art is based on images.
qs.a: Graffiti is often words; street art is based on images.
qs.why: "'Graffiti' often appears as words... 'Street art' is more based on images."

lessons.title: Oldest Pet Burial Ground in America
lessons.zh: 美国最古老的宠物墓地
lessons.sum: 纽约附近的哈茨代尔宠物公墓始于 1896 年，是美国仍在运营的最古老的宠物墓地，安葬着约 7 万只动物：猫、狗、蜥蜴、老鼠，甚至狮子幼崽和孟加拉虎。马克几乎每天都来看他的猫布茨，还打算将来和它葬在一起。

lines.en: On most days, Mark Lindenberg either drives or walks over to visit with Boots, his beloved cat who died in 2020 at 17 years old. The New York man had the animal buried at the Hartsdale Pet Cemetery, a burial place on small grassy hills near the main road.
lines.zh: 大多数日子里，马克·林登伯格都会开车或步行去看望布茨——他心爱的猫，2020 年 17 岁时去世。这位纽约人把它葬在了哈茨代尔宠物公墓，墓地位于主干道旁几座长满青草的小山上。

lines.en: The words on Boots' tombstone read, "You taught me how to love and be loved."
lines.zh: 布茨的墓碑上写着：“是你教会了我爱与被爱。”

lines.en: Other tombstones include phrases such as "A truer friend we never had" and "Our beloved queen."
lines.zh: 其他墓碑上写着“我们从没有过更真诚的朋友”“我们心爱的女王”之类的话。

lines.en: "Human cemeteries are sad," Lindenberg said. "This is one of the most cheerful places."
lines.zh: “人的墓地让人难过，”林登伯格说，“这里却是最让人愉快的地方之一。”

lines.en: He added, "I can't think of a better place."
lines.zh: 他还说：“我想不出比这更好的地方了。”

lines.en: Hartsdale is America's oldest pet cemetery in operation. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2012. Lindenberg says he paid about $7,000 to bury Boots at Hartsdale. Those costs cover the individual site, burial, burial container, tombstone, and grounds care.
lines.zh: 哈茨代尔是美国仍在运营的最古老的宠物墓地，2012 年被列入《国家史迹名录》。林登伯格说，他花了约 7000 美元把布茨葬在哈茨代尔，费用包括单独的墓地、安葬、棺木、墓碑和场地维护。

lines.en: "What have I worked for if I'm not going to do the things that matter most, and this mattered most," Lindenberg said. "I got instant closure the day I decided I was going to bury her here."
lines.zh: “如果不去做最重要的事，我工作是为了什么？而这件事最重要，”林登伯格说，“我决定把她葬在这里的那天，心里一下子就释然了。”

lines.en: Pet burials started in Hartsdale in 1896 when animal doctor Samuel Johnson let a woman bury her dog on his property of apple trees. The place is about 30 kilometers north of New York City.
lines.zh: 1896 年，兽医塞缪尔·约翰逊让一位女士把她的狗葬在自己的苹果园里，哈茨代尔的宠物安葬就这样开始了。这个地方在纽约市以北约 30 公里。

lines.en: Since that time, about 70,000 animals have been laid to rest in the two-hectare cemetery. Most of the pets buried at Hartsdale are cats and dogs, but several other kinds of animals are also there.
lines.zh: 从那以后，这座两公顷的墓地已安葬了约 7 万只动物。葬在哈茨代尔的宠物大多是猫和狗，但也有好几种别的动物。

lines.en: "There's reptiles that are buried here. Mice," said Edward Martin III, vice president of the Hartsdale Pet Cemetery. "There's a lion cub that was buried here in 1912 by a Russian princess. There's the ashes of Ming, who's a Bengal tiger that was buried here a few years ago. There are some monkeys."
lines.zh: “这里葬着爬行动物，还有老鼠，”哈茨代尔宠物公墓副总裁爱德华·马丁三世说，“有一只狮子幼崽，是 1912 年一位俄国公主葬在这里的。还有几年前安葬在这里的孟加拉虎‘明’的骨灰。还有一些猴子。”

lines.en: There is also Hudson the horse, some birds and singer Mariah Carey's cat, Clarence. The oldest headstone, dating to 1898, remembers the life of a dog named Blague.
lines.zh: 这里还有马儿哈德森、一些鸟，以及歌手玛丽亚·凯莉的猫克拉伦斯。最古老的墓碑可追溯到 1898 年，纪念一只叫布拉格的狗。

lines.en: Martin operates the place with his father Edward Martin Jr., who purchased the cemetery in 1974. The younger Martin is a lawyer and accountant who decided later in his career to help run the cemetery. He had worked there also as a teenager.
lines.zh: 马丁和父亲小爱德华·马丁一起经营这里。父亲在 1974 年买下了这座墓地。年轻的马丁是律师和会计师，在职业生涯后期决定来帮忙经营墓地，他十几岁时也在这里干过活。

lines.en: "I've seen what people go through, and they lose their pets, and I feel like I'm in a good position where I can help them," he said. "And I have helped them, and it makes me want to continue helping them."
lines.zh: “我见过人们失去宠物时的痛苦，我觉得自己处在一个能帮助他们的好位置，”他说，“我也确实帮助过他们，这让我想继续帮下去。”

lines.en: Between 250 and 300 burials take place at Hartsdale each year. The cemetery never runs out of space because not all of the burial sites are permanent. People can make a one-time forever maintenance payment of $3,500 or a yearly payment of $105. If the yearly payments stop, that gravesite is offered for sale.
lines.zh: 哈茨代尔每年有 250 到 300 次安葬。墓地永远不会没有空间，因为并不是所有墓位都是永久的。人们可以一次性支付 3500 美元的永久维护费，或者每年支付 105 美元。如果年费停付，这个墓位就会出售。

lines.en: "The pet in the grave will be removed from that plot so someone else who wants it can pay the maintenance. And the pets are taken out, and they're cremated, and they don't leave the cemetery," said Martin Jr., Hartsdale's president. "Their remains are scattered over the cemetery grass."
lines.zh: “墓里的宠物会被移出那块墓地，这样想要它的人就可以付维护费。宠物被移出后会火化，但不会离开墓地，”哈茨代尔总裁小马丁说，“它们的骨灰会撒在墓地的草地上。”

lines.en: A centerpiece at the cemetery is the war dog memorial at the top of a hill. Established in 1923, the memorial honored World War I service dogs. But these days, the memorial honors service dogs of all kinds.
lines.zh: 墓地的核心是山顶上的军犬纪念碑。纪念碑建于 1923 年，起初纪念第一次世界大战中服役的军犬，如今纪念各种各样的工作犬。

lines.en: Although Hartsdale is mostly a resting place for animals, the cremated remains of about 800 humans are buried here with their pets. There is a Martin family plot, where the elder Martin plans to be laid to rest when he dies.
lines.zh: 虽然哈茨代尔主要是动物的安息之地，但这里也和宠物一起安葬着约 800 人的骨灰。这里有马丁家族的墓地，老马丁打算去世后葬在这里。

lines.en: "I have to be buried somewhere. And why would I go to any place other than this?" he said. "My mother and father, and my mother-in-law or father-in-law are buried here, and so, that's a good reason by itself to do it."
lines.zh: “我总得葬在某个地方。我为什么要去别的地方呢？”他说，“我的父母、岳父岳母都葬在这里，单凭这一点就是个好理由。”

lines.en: Lindenberg also likes the idea. He has already prepared to be cremated and buried alongside Boots when the time comes.
lines.zh: 林登伯格也喜欢这个主意。他已经准备好，到时候火化后葬在布茨旁边。

lines.en: "I'm single. I don't know if I'll ever get married, and I can't think of a better place," he said. "I lived with my cat every day for almost 17 years. Why stop now?"
lines.zh: “我单身，不知道会不会结婚，我想不出更好的地方了，”他说，“我和我的猫天天在一起生活了快 17 年。为什么现在要停下呢？”

lines.en: In the meantime, Lindenberg, who lives a 10-minute walk away, will continue to visit his old friend almost daily.
lines.zh: 在那之前，住在步行 10 分钟远的林登伯格会继续几乎每天来看望他的老朋友。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: When did pet burials start at Hartsdale?
qs.why: "Pet burials started in Hartsdale in 1896."

qs.q: Why does the cemetery never run out of space?
opts: Not all burial sites are permanent.
qs.a: Not all burial sites are permanent.
qs.why: "not all of the burial sites are permanent."

qs.q: What does Lindenberg plan to do?
qs.why: "He has already prepared to be cremated and buried alongside Boots."

lessons.title: Setting Records on Guinness World Records Day
lessons.zh: 吉尼斯世界纪录日上的破纪录
lessons.sum: 2021 年 11 月 17 日是第 18 个吉尼斯世界纪录日，各国挑战者纷纷破纪录：英国体操运动员后空翻 6 米、委内瑞拉女足球员一天破两项纪录、中国小伙倒立走着拉汽车、美国人踩弹跳杆跳过五辆伦敦出租车。吉尼斯纪录的起源是一场关于“最快的猎鸟”的争论。

lines.en: November 17, 2021 marks the eighteenth yearly Guinness World Records Day.
lines.zh: 2021 年 11 月 17 日是第 18 个一年一度的吉尼斯世界纪录日。

lines.en: People from around the world are trying to set all kinds of records on this day. They include records for most football crossovers while sitting down to most consecutive jumps over cars on a pogo stick.
lines.zh: 这一天，世界各地的人们都在尝试创造各种各样的纪录，从坐着做最多的足球“绕球”动作，到踩弹跳杆连续跳过最多的汽车。

lines.en: British gymnast Ashley Watson said, "If you want to be a Guinness World Records title holder just go for it." Watson broke his own record on gymnastics equipment for "farthest backflip between horizontal bars" with a distance of six meters. He set the previous record of 5.87 meters back in 2018.
lines.zh: 英国体操运动员阿什利·沃森说：“如果你想成为吉尼斯世界纪录保持者，那就放手去做。”沃森在体操器械上打破了自己保持的“单杠间最远后空翻”纪录，距离达 6 米。他之前的纪录是 2018 年创下的 5.87 米。

lines.en: Venezuelan soccer player Laura Biondo broke not one but two records for the day. She recorded "most sit-down football crossovers in 30 seconds (female)" with 62 and "most double around the world ball control tricks in one minute (female)" with 24. The two new records added to Biondo's 11 other Guinness records. Soccer is the American word for the sport of football.
lines.zh: 委内瑞拉足球运动员劳拉·比翁多这一天打破了不止一项、而是两项纪录。她创下了“30 秒内坐姿足球绕球次数最多（女子）”纪录，共 62 次；以及“一分钟内双环绕控球技巧次数最多（女子）”纪录，共 24 次。这两项新纪录使比翁多的吉尼斯纪录又多了两项，此前她已有 11 项。Soccer 是美国人对“足球”这项运动的叫法。

lines.en: Biondo said, "If you set yourself a goal, you can definitely achieve it if you put hard work into it." She is planning to set a few more records to reach a total of at least 15.
lines.zh: 比翁多说：“如果你给自己定一个目标，只要你努力，就一定能实现。”她计划再创几项纪录，总数至少达到 15 项。

lines.en: The idea for Guinness World Records came in the early 1950s when some hunters in Wexford, Ireland argued about the fastest game bird. They could not find the answer in any book. So Hugh Beaver came up with an idea for a book to settle the arguments and to publicize his beer company, Guinness. The book had sold 143 million copies by 2019. There are now television programs, game shows and museums to show the records.
lines.zh: 吉尼斯世界纪录的想法诞生于 20 世纪 50 年代初。当时爱尔兰韦克斯福德的一些猎人争论哪种猎鸟飞得最快，在任何书里都找不到答案。于是休·比弗想出了一个主意：出一本书来平息这类争论，同时为他的啤酒公司吉尼斯做宣传。到 2019 年，这本书已售出 1.43 亿册。如今还有电视节目、游戏节目和博物馆来展示这些纪录。

lines.en: In case you are wondering, Guinness says the fastest game bird is the golden plover.
lines.zh: 你要是好奇的话，吉尼斯说最快的猎鸟是金斑鸻。

lines.en: A few more records were also set Wednesday on World Records Day.
lines.zh: 星期三的世界纪录日上还创下了另外几项纪录。

lines.en: In Nanchong, China, Zhang Shuang, who weighs 70 kilograms, pulled a 1225-kilogram vehicle while walking on his hands. He was able to pass the 50-meter mark in 1 minute 13.27 seconds. That was good enough for the "fastest time to pull a car 50 meters walking on hands."
lines.zh: 在中国南充，体重 70 公斤的张爽用手倒立行走，拉动了一辆 1225 公斤重的汽车。他用 1 分 13.27 秒走过了 50 米，创下了“倒立行走拉车 50 米最快用时”纪录。

lines.en: Zhang said he is walking on his hands every day and often shows them off to his students.
lines.zh: 张爽说他每天都倒立行走，还经常给学生们表演。

lines.en: In southeastern China, 11-year-old Wang Guanwutong failed in his first attempt to set the record for "most consecutive breakdance airflares (male)." An airflare is a dance movement in which the dancer spins around the dance floor on one hand.
lines.zh: 在中国东南部，11 岁的王冠武彤第一次尝试“连续霹雳舞托马斯全旋次数最多（男子）”纪录时失败了。托马斯全旋是一种舞蹈动作，舞者用一只手撑地在舞池上旋转。

lines.en: Wang finally set a new record for males of 94 airflares. However, he has a long way to go to match the female record of 121 airflares set by seven-year-old Qi Yufan, also of China.
lines.zh: 王冠武彤最终以 94 次创下了男子新纪录。不过，要追上同样来自中国的 7 岁女孩齐雨凡创下的 121 次女子纪录，他还有很长的路要走。

lines.en: In Japan, Takahiro Ikeda set not one but three records on his BMX bicycle. Those records are: "most BMX Stick B in 30 seconds," 3; "most BMX time machines in 30 seconds," 45; and "BMX - most turbine megaspins in one minute:" 45.
lines.zh: 在日本，池田贵广骑 BMX 小轮车创下了不止一项、而是三项纪录：“30 秒内 BMX Stick B 最多次数”3 次，“30 秒内 BMX 时光机最多次数”45 次，以及“BMX 一分钟内涡轮大旋转最多次数”45 次。

lines.en: If you don't know what they are, don't try them.
lines.zh: 如果你不知道这些是什么，就别去尝试。

lines.en: In Doha, Qatar, Ayoub Touabe of Morocco used one of his legs instead of his hands to set the record for "most single leg backward somersaults in 30 seconds." He completed 12 while standing on one leg.
lines.zh: 在卡塔尔多哈，摩洛哥人阿尤布·图阿贝用一条腿而不是双手，创下了“30 秒内单腿后空翻最多次数”纪录。他单腿站立完成了 12 次。

lines.en: In Britain, an American set his own record for "most consecutive cars jumped over on a pogo stick."
lines.zh: 在英国，一位美国人刷新了自己保持的“踩弹跳杆连续跳过最多汽车”纪录。

lines.en: Tyler Phillips used a pogo stick, a kind of toy used for jumping up and down, to jump over five London Black taxicabs to beat the old record of four. Each taxicab car is nearly 2 meters tall and 1.6 meter wide.
lines.zh: 泰勒·菲利普斯用弹跳杆——一种用来上下跳的玩具——跳过了五辆伦敦黑色出租车，打破了原来四辆的纪录。每辆出租车都将近 2 米高、1.6 米宽。

lines.en: He said, "Training for this record was way harder than actually doing it."
lines.zh: 他说：“为这个纪录训练，比真正去跳难多了。”

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

qs.q: How did the idea for Guinness World Records begin?
opts: Hunters argued about the fastest game bird.
A soccer player asked for it.
qs.a: Hunters argued about the fastest game bird.
qs.why: "some hunters in Wexford, Ireland argued about the fastest game bird."

qs.q: What is the fastest game bird?
qs.why: "the fastest game bird is the golden plover."

qs.q: How many taxicabs did Tyler Phillips jump over?
qs.why: "to jump over five London Black taxicabs."

lessons.title: What Americans Are Dressing Up as on Halloween
lessons.zh: 谷歌：美国人万圣节都扮成什么？
lessons.sum: 谷歌的 Frightgeist 网站根据搜索数据列出美国最受欢迎的万圣节装扮：女巫、兔子和恐龙排前三，其后是蜘蛛侠和《101 斑点狗》里的库伊拉。网站还能推荐冷门装扮，并用地图显示各地最流行的打扮。

lines.en: Here is a question for our listeners: What do witches, rabbits and dinosaurs have in common?
lines.zh: 问听众朋友们一个问题：女巫、兔子和恐龙有什么共同点？

lines.en: The answer? They are the top three most popular Halloween costumes this year in the United States. That information comes from data gathered by the Google News Initiative.
lines.zh: 答案是：它们是今年美国最受欢迎的三种万圣节装扮。这一信息来自“谷歌新闻倡议”收集的数据。

lines.en: A special website called "Google Frightgeist" provides a look at the 500 most popular costumes this year nationwide. It also lets users know what costumes they are likely to see where they live on Halloween night.
lines.zh: 一个叫“谷歌 Frightgeist”的专门网站展示了今年全美最受欢迎的 500 种装扮，还能让用户知道万圣节晚上在自己住的地方可能会看到哪些装扮。

lines.en: Rounding out the top five most-searched costumes this year are the superhero Spider-man and Cruella De Vil, a dog-hating character from the Disney movie The Hundred and One Dalmatians. The 2021 films Cruella and Spider-Man: No Way Home are surely behind the popularity of these costumes.
lines.zh: 今年搜索最多的前五名装扮，另外两个是超级英雄蜘蛛侠，以及迪士尼电影《101 斑点狗》里讨厌狗的角色库伊拉·德维尔。2021 年上映的电影《库伊拉》和《蜘蛛侠：英雄无归》无疑是这两种装扮走红的原因。

lines.en: Frightgeist offers more than just lists of the year's most popular costumes. It also aims to help people who do not yet know what they are going to dress up as for Halloween. And it provides suggestions for people who hope to stand out with unusual and rare costume choices.
lines.zh: Frightgeist 提供的不只是今年最受欢迎装扮的榜单。它还想帮助那些还没决定万圣节扮成什么的人，并为希望用不寻常、少见的装扮脱颖而出的人提供建议。

lines.en: Users can choose "show me something less popular" or "surprise me" to get truly unusual costume ideas.
lines.zh: 用户可以选择“给我看不那么流行的”或者“给我个惊喜”，得到真正与众不同的装扮主意。

lines.en: For example, if you choose "witch" on the website but are looking to dress up as something less common, Frightgeist suggests ideas like "Tin Man" and "Candy Corn." The Tin Man is a character from the film and book The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. Frightgeist says it is the 339th most popular costume in America. It notes that you have a "shockingly low chance of running into another Tin Man costume at a party." Candy corn is a sweet food that looks like a piece of corn. It is a common thing to eat during the Halloween season. But it is a decidedly uncommon costume.
lines.zh: 比如，如果你在网站上选了“女巫”，但想扮成不那么常见的东西，Frightgeist 会推荐“铁皮人”和“玉米糖”之类的主意。铁皮人是电影和小说《绿野仙踪》里的角色。Frightgeist 说它是美国第 339 受欢迎的装扮，并指出你在派对上“碰到另一个铁皮人的几率低得惊人”。玉米糖是一种看起来像玉米粒的糖果，是万圣节期间常吃的东西，但作为装扮可绝对不常见。

lines.en: The site's "costume map" gives users a look at the most popular costumes in cities across America. For example, the top costume around Charleston, South Carolina, is an astronaut. In the northernmost part of Maine, an elephant appears to be a popular choice. And in Topeka, Kansas, you might find a frightening number of zombies wandering the streets on Halloween.
lines.zh: 网站的“装扮地图”让用户看到美国各城市最受欢迎的装扮。比如，南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿一带最受欢迎的装扮是宇航员；在缅因州最北部，大象似乎很受欢迎；而在堪萨斯州托皮卡，万圣节夜里你可能会看到多得吓人的僵尸在街上游荡。

lines.en: To see more costume information and to get ideas for yourself, you can visit frightgeist.withgoogle.com.
lines.zh: 想看更多装扮信息、给自己找灵感，可以访问 frightgeist.withgoogle.com。

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: What are the top three Halloween costumes this year?
qs.why: "They are the top three most popular Halloween costumes."

qs.q: What does Frightgeist suggest for an unusual costume?
qs.why: "Frightgeist suggests ideas like 'Tin Man' and 'Candy Corn.'"

qs.q: What is the top costume around Charleston, South Carolina?
qs.why: "the top costume around Charleston, South Carolina, is an astronaut."

lessons.title: Is There a Doctor in the House?
lessons.zh: 谁可以被称为“博士/医生”？
lessons.sum: 吉尔·拜登拥有教育学博士学位，常被称为“Dr. Jill Biden”。一篇评论文章认为只有医生才配叫 Dr.，引发热议。英语里 Dr. 既可称医生也可称博士；西班牙语、土耳其语类似，越南语和汉语则用不同的词区分。美国大多数新闻机构的写作规范只对医生用 Dr.。

lines.en: The next first lady of the United States, Jill Biden, holds a doctorate in education. She completed her degree from the University of Delaware in 2007. When President-elect Joe Biden takes office next month, Jill Biden will be the first-ever first lady with a doctoral degree.
lines.zh: 美国下一任第一夫人吉尔·拜登拥有教育学博士学位，她 2007 年在特拉华大学获得这个学位。当选总统乔·拜登下个月就职后，吉尔·拜登将成为有史以来第一位拥有博士学位的第一夫人。

lines.en: She is widely known as "Dr. Jill Biden." This is not unusual. In English, the word "Doctor" (Dr.) can appear before the name of a person who holds a doctoral degree or a medical degree.
lines.zh: 她通常被称为“Dr. Jill Biden”（吉尔·拜登博士）。这并不稀奇。在英语里，Doctor（Dr.）可以放在拥有博士学位或医学学位的人名字前面。

lines.en: But a recent opinion article published in the Wall Street Journal newspaper disagreed with the custom. The title of the article, by American writer Joseph Epstein, is "Is There a Doctor in the White House? Not if You Need an M.D."
lines.zh: 但最近《华尔街日报》发表的一篇评论文章对这个惯例提出了异议。文章作者是美国作家约瑟夫·爱泼斯坦，标题是《白宫里有医生吗？如果你需要的是医学博士，那就没有》。

lines.en: "M.D." is short for a doctor of medicine.
lines.zh: “M.D.”是医学博士的缩写。

lines.en: Epstein begins his article like this: "Madame First Lady--Mrs. Biden--Jill-- kiddo: a bit of advice on what may seem like a small but I think is a not unimportant matter. Any chance you might drop the "Dr. before your name?
lines.zh: 爱泼斯坦这样开头：“第一夫人女士——拜登夫人——吉尔——小家伙：就一件看似小事、但我认为并非不重要的事给你一点建议。你能不能把名字前的‘Dr.’去掉？”

lines.en: Epstein argues that Jill Biden does not deserve to be called "Dr. Biden" because she is not a medical doctor. He notes, "A wise man once said that no one should call himself "Dr." unless he has delivered a child."
lines.zh: 爱泼斯坦认为，吉尔·拜登不该被称为“拜登博士”，因为她不是医生。他写道：“一位智者曾说，没接生过孩子的人，不该自称‘Dr.’。”

lines.en: Reaction to the article came quickly.
lines.zh: 对这篇文章的反应来得很快。

lines.en: Supporters of Epstein's argument agreed that people with "teaching degrees" should not want people to call them "Doctor." One conservative television presenter, Tucker Carlson, said Dr. Biden is as much of a doctor as Dr. Pepper is. Dr. Pepper is a popular brand of soft drink.
lines.zh: 支持爱泼斯坦观点的人同意，拥有“教育学位”的人不应该希望别人称自己为“Doctor”。保守派电视主持人塔克·卡尔森说，拜登博士是“博士”的程度，就跟“胡椒博士”一样。胡椒博士（Dr. Pepper）是一个流行的汽水品牌。

lines.en: Critics of Epstein's article, however, expressed surprise that the Wall Street Journal let such a story be published. They said they found it to be offensive, sexist and, more simply, pointless.
lines.zh: 然而，批评爱泼斯坦文章的人对《华尔街日报》竟允许发表这样的文章表示惊讶。他们说觉得这篇文章冒犯人、有性别歧视，说白了就是毫无意义。

lines.en: In a post on Instagram, former first lady Michelle Obama wrote: "Right now, we're all seeing what happens to so many professional women, whether their titles are Dr., Ms., Mrs., or even First Lady: All too often, our accomplishments are met with skepticism, even derision."
lines.zh: 前第一夫人米歇尔·奥巴马在 Instagram 上写道：“此刻，我们都看到许多职业女性的遭遇，不管她们的头衔是博士、女士、夫人，甚至是第一夫人：我们的成就太常遭到怀疑，甚至嘲笑。”

lines.en: Another former first lady, Hillary Clinton, used fewer words. She tweeted: "Her name is Dr. Jill Biden. Get used to it."
lines.zh: 另一位前第一夫人希拉里·克林顿说得更简短。她发推文说：“她的名字是吉尔·拜登博士。习惯吧。”

lines.en: Vice President-elect Kamala Harris reacted to the article during a television appearance this week, saying, "It's not the American way."
lines.zh: 当选副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯本周在一次电视节目中回应了这篇文章，说：“这不是美国的方式。”

lines.en: Jill Biden offered her own response Thursday, when she and President-elect Biden appeared on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. She said the Epstein article surprised her. She said her doctoral degree is one of the things that she is most proud of. She added, "I worked so hard for it."
lines.zh: 吉尔·拜登星期四和当选总统拜登一起上《斯蒂芬·科尔伯特深夜秀》时作出了回应。她说爱泼斯坦的文章让她很意外。她说，博士学位是她最自豪的事情之一。她还说：“我为它付出了那么多努力。”

lines.en: Around the world, social media users who hold doctoral degrees in fields such as history, education and mathematics changed their Twitter names to include "Dr."
lines.zh: 在世界各地，拥有历史、教育、数学等领域博士学位的社交媒体用户纷纷把自己的推特名字改成带“Dr.”的。

lines.en: In professional situations, it is correct to use the title "Doctor" for medical doctors as well as for people who have earned doctoral degrees. The lowercase form of the word, "doctor," is only used to describe a person who is trained and licensed to treat sick and injured people.
lines.zh: 在职业场合，对医生以及获得博士学位的人使用“Doctor”这个头衔都是正确的。小写的 doctor 只用来指受过训练、有执照为病人和伤者治疗的人。

lines.en: Jill Biden's students call her "Dr. B." At political events, she is introduced as "Dr. Jill Biden." Her Twitter account is @DrBiden. The general belief is that anyone who has earned a doctoral degree has the right to have the honorific "Dr." before their name.
lines.zh: 吉尔·拜登的学生叫她“B 博士”。在政治活动上，她被介绍为“吉尔·拜登博士”。她的推特账号是 @DrBiden。普遍的看法是，任何获得博士学位的人都有权在名字前加上“Dr.”这个敬称。

lines.en: But, what about in other languages?
lines.zh: 那其他语言呢？

lines.en: Many are similar to English. In Spanish, for example, "Doctor" is used for people with medical degrees and doctoral degrees in other fields.
lines.zh: 很多语言和英语类似。比如在西班牙语里，Doctor 既用于有医学学位的人，也用于其他领域有博士学位的人。

lines.en: Claudia Bautista, a VOA Learning English listener from Mexico City, explains:
lines.zh: 来自墨西哥城的 VOA 慢速英语听众克劳迪娅·包蒂斯塔解释说：

lines.en: "In my city, the governor in chief is Dra. Claudia Sheinbaum. All people, colleagues, news…call her Dra. Sheinbaum. She is a politician, activist, writer and scientist, with a doctoral degree, that's why we call her Doctor (or Doctora)."
lines.zh: “在我们城市，首席长官是克劳迪娅·辛鲍姆博士（Dra.）。所有人——同事、新闻……都称她辛鲍姆博士。她是政治家、社会活动家、作家和科学家，有博士学位，所以我们称她 Doctor（或 Doctora）。”

lines.en: In Spanish, the feminine form of Doctor is "Doctora."
lines.zh: 在西班牙语里，Doctor 的阴性形式是 Doctora。

lines.en: It is much the same in Turkish, as VOA Learning English listener Cem Utkan explains:
lines.zh: 土耳其语也差不多，VOA 慢速英语听众杰姆·乌特坎解释说：

lines.en: "Dr. is placed before the names of people who have completed their doctorate education and have the title of doctor," Utkan said. The same word is also used for medical doctors.
lines.zh: “Dr. 放在完成博士教育、拥有博士头衔的人名字前面。”乌特坎说。同一个词也用于医生。

lines.en: Some languages, such as Vietnamese and Chinese, use different honorifics for the two kinds of "Doctors." San Dao, a listener from Vietnam whose second language is English, explains:
lines.zh: 有些语言，比如越南语和汉语，对这两种“Doctor”用不同的敬称。来自越南、以英语为第二语言的听众圣道解释说：

lines.en: "Vietnamese uses "bác sĩ" (doctor) to address medical doctors who work in hospitals, dentists, or maybe veterinarians or physician. But one point worth saying is that "bác sĩ" is not an honorific for those who have completed their Ph.D. A Ph.D holder is called "tiến sĩ" which can be clearly distinguished from "bác sĩ."
lines.zh: “越南语用‘bác sĩ’（医生）称呼在医院工作的医生、牙医，或许还有兽医或内科医生。但值得一提的是，‘bác sĩ’不是给读完博士的人的敬称。拥有博士学位的人叫‘tiến sĩ’，这和‘bác sĩ’区分得很清楚。”

lines.en: San adds, "I believe everyone knows the next first lady is not a medical doctor. So there's no point in clarifying it."
lines.zh: 圣道还说：“我相信大家都知道下一任第一夫人不是医生，所以没必要特意澄清。”

lines.en: As Epstein's opinion article and reaction to it went viral, the American dictionary Merriam-Webster offered a bit of language history. It wrote on Twitter: "The word 'doctor' comes from the Latin word for 'teacher."
lines.zh: 随着爱泼斯坦的评论文章和各方反应在网上疯传，美国词典《韦氏词典》讲了一点语言历史。它在推特上写道：“doctor 这个词来自拉丁语中表示‘老师’的词。”

lines.en: You probably already know that VOA Learning English has a "Dr. Jill" of its own. That would be language learning specialist Jill Robbins, who earned a doctorate in applied linguistics from Georgetown University. Around the office – when we are there – many of us call her "Dr. Jill."
lines.zh: 你可能已经知道，VOA 慢速英语也有自己的“吉尔博士”，那就是语言学习专家吉尔·罗宾斯，她在乔治城大学获得了应用语言学博士学位。在办公室里——我们在办公室的时候——很多人叫她“吉尔博士”。

lines.en: Yet, it is VOA's own writing style -- and the writing style of most American news organizations -- to only use "Dr." before someone's name if they are a medical doctor. That is why we call the nation's top infectious disease expert "Dr. Anthony Fauci" but do not use the honorific "Dr." when writing about Jill Biden.
lines.zh: 不过，按照 VOA 自己的写作规范——也是大多数美国新闻机构的写作规范——只有医生才在名字前加“Dr.”。所以我们称全国顶尖的传染病专家为“安东尼·福奇医生”（Dr. Anthony Fauci），而写吉尔·拜登时不用“Dr.”这个敬称。

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

lines.en: And I'm Jill Robbins.
lines.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

qs.q: In English, who can use "Dr." before their name?
opts: people with a doctoral or medical degree
qs.a: people with a doctoral or medical degree
qs.why: "the word 'Doctor' (Dr.) can appear before the name of a person who holds a doctoral degree or a medical degree."

qs.q: Where does the word "doctor" come from?
qs.why: "The word 'doctor' comes from the Latin word for 'teacher.'"

qs.q: In VOA's writing style, when is "Dr." used?
qs.why: "only use 'Dr.' before someone's name if they are a medical doctor."

lessons.title: Younger Americans Not Interested in Tiffany Jewelry, Gap Clothes
lessons.zh: 美国年轻人对蒂芙尼、Gap 不感兴趣了
lessons.sum: 蒂芙尼、Gap、哈雷戴维森这些曾受追捧的品牌，正在失去 20 多岁、30 多岁的千禧一代顾客；而塔吉特通过引入天然食品和设计师服装重获青睐。千禧一代想要新鲜事物和体验，看重“真实”有个性的品牌，也很重视方便。

lines.en: In the United States, some once-loved stores are trying to understand decreasing sales. Jewelry store Tiffany & Co. is an example. Clothing store the Gap, and motorcycle store Harley Davidson are others. These three are more than shopping places – they are brands, public images strongly linked with an object or person.
lines.zh: 在美国，一些曾经深受喜爱的商店正在努力弄明白销量为什么下滑。珠宝店蒂芙尼就是一个例子，服装店 Gap 和摩托车店哈雷戴维森也是。这三家不只是购物场所——它们是品牌，是与某种物品或人紧密相连的公众形象。

lines.en: But today's younger Americans in their 20s and 30s are not as interested in buying things from these brands as their parents were. Instead, a store like Target has gained the attention and money of many so-called Millennials, people who became adults in the 21st century.
lines.zh: 可是如今二三十岁的美国年轻人，不像他们的父母那样热衷于买这些品牌的东西。相反，像塔吉特（Target）这样的商店赢得了许多所谓“千禧一代”——在 21 世纪成年的人——的关注和钱包。

lines.en: Target has been around for more than 50 years. Today, it is the 8th largest seller in the country. One reason is because it has changed its stores for a new generation of shoppers. For example, it started offering more natural foods and designer clothing. It also created a showroom for the latest kinds of things for the home.
lines.zh: 塔吉特已有 50 多年历史，如今是全国第八大零售商。原因之一是它为新一代顾客改造了门店。比如，它开始提供更多天然食品和设计师服装，还设立了一个展示最新家居用品的展厅。

lines.en: Target's success shows that the in-store experience remains important. While many Americans are shopping online, just 11 percent of retail sales are done on the internet. That means 89 percent of buying is done in the traditional way: walking into a store, reports the United States Department of Commerce.
lines.zh: 塔吉特的成功表明，店内购物体验仍然很重要。美国商务部报告说，虽然很多美国人在网上购物，但只有 11% 的零售额是在网上完成的。也就是说，89% 的购买是以传统方式完成的：走进商店。

lines.en: "Target was really stuck… and, all the sudden, was able to again drive growth with millennials," says Jason Dorsey. He is president and millennial expert at the Center for Generational Kinetics.
lines.zh: “塔吉特原本真的停滞不前了……突然之间，它又能靠千禧一代推动增长了。”杰森·多尔西说。他是代际动力学中心的总裁和千禧一代专家。

lines.en: Target noticed that millennials shop differently from their parents. Since they are the country's largest living generation, they are important for retailers.
lines.zh: 塔吉特注意到，千禧一代购物的方式和父母不同。由于他们是美国在世人口最多的一代，对零售商很重要。

lines.en: They want new things, not the old brands they grew up knowing. They also want adventure and experiences. Finally, they are very concerned with brands that feel authentic.
lines.zh: 他们想要新东西，而不是从小就知道的老品牌。他们还想要冒险和体验。最后，他们非常在意品牌是否让人感觉“真实”。

lines.en: Dorsey said, "What millennials tell us is that an authentic brand…has a personality. The brand itself has …values." He added that millennials also value convenience.
lines.zh: 多尔西说：“千禧一代告诉我们，一个真实的品牌……有个性，品牌本身有……价值观。”他还说，千禧一代也很看重方便。

lines.en: Millennials are expected to be big spenders over the next ten years. In that time, they will begin to buy things for new homes and start having children. Brands that fail to appeal to these important young shoppers can quickly find themselves in trouble.
lines.zh: 预计未来十年千禧一代会是消费大户。在这期间，他们会开始为新家添置东西、开始生孩子。不能吸引这些重要年轻顾客的品牌，很快就会陷入困境。

lines.en: Millennials will not buy old brands "that they think don't really understand or get them," Dorsey says. He says retailers that sell items that seem to be special are likely to do well.
lines.zh: 多尔西说，千禧一代不会买那些“他们认为并不真正理解他们”的老品牌。他说，卖那些看起来很特别的商品的零售商很可能会做得好。

lines.en: In contrast, millennials have not shown much interest in the costly jewelry sold by Tiffany. The 200-year-old brand is now being sold to a French company.
lines.zh: 相比之下，千禧一代对蒂芙尼卖的昂贵珠宝没表现出多大兴趣。这个有 200 年历史的品牌现在正被卖给一家法国公司。

lines.en: At Harley Davidson, sales of motorcycles have been decreasing since 2014. The brand once represented freedom and the possibilities of the open road. Now, young people want to use ride-sharing companies to move around.
lines.zh: 哈雷戴维森的摩托车销量从 2014 年起一直在下降。这个品牌曾经代表着自由和公路旅行的无限可能。如今，年轻人想用网约车出行。

lines.en: And most young people today do not shop at the Gap, whose clothes were once so common they looked like a uniform for Americans in their 20s.
lines.zh: 如今大多数年轻人也不在 Gap 买衣服了。曾几何时，Gap 的衣服普遍到看起来像是二十几岁美国人的“制服”。

lines.en: "You know millennials are the most photographed generation of adults in history," Dorsey said.
lines.zh: “你知道吗，千禧一代是历史上被拍照最多的一代成年人。”多尔西说。

lines.en: In those photographs, they want to send a message, Dorsey explained. They want to show that they buy from stores that treat people well, and are good for the environment.
lines.zh: 多尔西解释说，他们想通过这些照片传达一个信息：他们在善待员工、对环境有益的商店买东西。

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

qs.q: Which store gained the attention of many Millennials?
qs.why: "a store like Target has gained the attention and money of many so-called Millennials."

qs.q: What percent of retail sales are done online?
qs.why: "just 11 percent of retail sales are done on the internet."

qs.q: What do Millennials want from a brand?
opts: to feel authentic, with personality and values
qs.a: to feel authentic, with personality and values
qs.why: "an authentic brand…has a personality."

lessons.title: Teen Service Group Aims to Help Others and Better Themselves
lessons.zh: 青少年志愿服务：帮助别人，也成就自己
lessons.sum: 基督教援助组织 Group Cares 每年派几百名青少年到全美各地，利用一周暑假免费为有需要的人修房子。在马里兰州塞文，他们为退休的凯特修楼梯、刷油漆。孩子们走出舒适区，学会合作、沟通和同理心。

lines.en: Kate Snyder has been living in the same house in Severn, Maryland, for more than 18 years. "I raised my son here. It was a beautiful place to raise a child. Now, I'm on my own and still enjoying it."
lines.zh: 凯特·斯奈德在马里兰州塞文的同一栋房子里住了 18 年多。“我在这里把儿子养大。这是个养孩子的好地方。现在我一个人住，还是很享受。”

lines.en: But as the years pass, the house needs many repairs. Snyder, who is retired and still works two part-time jobs, does not have the money to pay for repairs.
lines.zh: 可是随着年头增长，房子需要大量修缮。斯奈德已经退休，仍在打两份兼职，没有钱付修理费。

lines.en: Enter Group Cares, a Christian-based aid organization.
lines.zh: 这时，基督教援助组织 Group Cares 出现了。

lines.en: Each year, the group sends hundreds of teenagers on service trips across the United States. The young people repair homes and provide other help. One such team of teens is spending a week repairing Snyder's house.
lines.zh: 这个组织每年派几百名青少年到美国各地进行服务之旅。年轻人修房子，并提供其他帮助。其中一支青少年队伍正花一周时间修斯奈德的房子。

lines.en: "They're going to put in new stairs for me," she said happily. "And it needed paint desperately."
lines.zh: “他们要给我装新楼梯，”她高兴地说，“房子也急需刷漆了。”

lines.en: Blocks away, other teens are working on Ursula Brett's home. They are removing wallpaper and preparing to paint the house.
lines.zh: 几个街区外，另一些青少年在乌苏拉·布雷特家干活，他们在揭墙纸，准备给房子刷漆。

lines.en: More than 400 teenagers from all over the U.S. take part in the service trips. They spend one week of their summer vacation fixing homes in the day, and sleeping on the floor of local Christian religious centers at night.
lines.zh: 来自美国各地的 400 多名青少年参加了服务之旅。他们用一周暑假，白天修房子，晚上睡在当地基督教宗教中心的地板上。

lines.en: Eric Lohe, spokesperson for Group Cares, says teens work at 30 sites. He says they work in groups of five and are guided and supervised by adult volunteers.
lines.zh: Group Cares 的发言人埃里克·洛赫说，青少年们在 30 个地点工作。他说，他们五人一组，由成年志愿者指导和监督。

lines.en: "We provide adult leaders who are always around on the sites helping students to be able to learn skills that they wouldn't necessarily have from home."
lines.zh: “我们安排成年领队一直在现场，帮助学生学习他们在家里不一定能学到的技能。”

lines.en: Both young people and adult volunteers raise money for the camp. Local people provide money as well.
lines.zh: 青少年和成年志愿者都为营地筹款，当地人也会出钱。

lines.en: It pays for food, sleep sites and material costs.
lines.zh: 这些钱用于支付食物、住宿和材料费用。

lines.en: Lohe says, "...When we come to a resident we can say, 'We're here to help you, to provide the repairs, but we're going to do that at no cost.'"
lines.zh: 洛赫说：“……我们来到一位居民家时可以说，‘我们来帮你修房子，而且是免费的。’”

lines.en: The teens working in homes in Severn were part of the Chesapeake Bay Camp. Director Barry Oren says they arrive as strangers.
lines.zh: 在塞文修房子的青少年属于“切萨皮克湾营”。营地负责人巴里·奥伦说，他们来的时候互不相识。

lines.en: "We put them in crews with people they['ve] never met before. Then, they go out and work on somebody's home they not only never met before, but also probably will never see again. The idea that they are stepping out of their comfort zone is huge for them," he said. "It gives them an opportunity to be part of the team. Very quickly, almost instantly, they learn how to do projects together."
lines.zh: “我们把他们和从没见过的人编在一组。然后他们去修一个不仅素不相识、而且很可能以后再也见不到的人的房子。走出舒适区，这对他们来说意义重大，”他说，“这给了他们成为团队一员的机会。很快，几乎是立刻，他们就学会了一起做项目。”

lines.en: This summer, the Chesapeake Bay Camp teens put in 7,650 service hours.
lines.zh: 今年夏天，切萨皮克湾营的青少年完成了 7650 小时的服务。

lines.en: "All of a sudden, it starts to make sense," Oren said.
lines.zh: “突然之间，一切都说得通了。”奥伦说。

lines.en: "'Oh, there are people who don't live like I do. There are people that I can help.' They're learning about how to communicate, how to express needs and wants, how to become empathetic."
lines.zh: “‘哦，原来有人和我过的生活不一样。有人是我可以帮助的。’他们在学习怎样沟通，怎样表达需要和想法，怎样变得有同理心。”

lines.en: The service group also holds two Christian religious services a day.
lines.zh: 这个服务团体每天还举行两次基督教礼拜。

lines.en: "We're really geared toward helping students, 12- through 17-year-olds, to be able to know God's love for them," Lohe said. "And to be able to share this love, not necessarily by preaching, but by showing that they care for people in the community."
lines.zh: “我们真正的目标是帮助 12 到 17 岁的学生了解上帝对他们的爱，”洛赫说，“并且能分享这份爱，不一定靠说教，而是通过表现出他们关心社区里的人。”

lines.en: Camp organizers say the free repairs help homeowners save money and provide the young people with a priceless experience.
lines.zh: 营地组织者说，免费修缮帮助房主省了钱，也给了年轻人无价的经历。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: What do the teens do on their service trips?
qs.why: "The young people repair homes and provide other help."

qs.q: Where do the teens sleep at night?
opts: on the floor of local Christian centers
qs.a: on the floor of local Christian centers
qs.why: "sleeping on the floor of local Christian religious centers at night."

qs.q: What does "stepping out of their comfort zone" mean here?
qs.why: 他们和陌生人一起为陌生人修房子。
